SidePanel

A panel that slides in from the start edge after a button — a navigation List, filters, a cart — built on the APG disclosure pattern (a button with aria-expanded controlling a region) rather than a modal dialog, with a modal option for when the page must be inert. On wide screens optionally a persistent sidebar.

Basic usage

Install the package:

pnpm add @design-schema/react

Import the stylesheet once for the app, then the component:

import '@design-schema/react/index.css';
import { SidePanel } from '@design-schema/react';

Examples

import { SidePanel, Button, Link, Stack } from '@design-schema/react';

const defaultBody = (
  <Stack element="nav" gap="tight">
    <Link href="#" label="Dashboard" />
    <Link href="#" label="Projects" />
    <Link href="#" label="Settings" />
  </Stack>
);

<SidePanel
  trigger={<Button label="Open menu" variant="secondary" />}
  heading="Menu"
>
  {defaultBody}
</SidePanel>

Props

PropTypeDefaultDescriptionPlatforms
triggercontent—

The Button that shows and hides the panel (usually `iconOnly` with the `menu` Icon and a label like "Menu"). It is the APG disclosure button: the panel sets aria-expanded and aria-controls on it, and it stays a toggle — pressing it again closes. Omit to control `open` from elsewhere (a Toolbar).

web, lit, rn, swiftui
openboolean—

Controlled visibility. Omit for uncontrolled (the trigger toggles it).

web, lit, rn, swiftui
heading requiredstring—

The panel's title and accessible name ("Menu", "Filters", "Your cart"). May be visually hidden with `hideHeading`.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
hideHeadingbooleanfalse

Keep the title for assistive technology but do not render it (a navigation panel whose List is self-explanatory).

Accessibility: The accessible name is required regardless.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
children requiredcontent—

The body: a List or Tree of Links for navigation, a Form of filters, a Stack of Cards. Scrolls inside the panel when taller than the viewport.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
footercontent—

Pinned to the bottom of the panel above the safe area (a sign-out Button, a "Apply filters" action row).

web, lit, rn, swiftui
sidestart | endstart

The edge the panel slides from: `start` is left in left-to-right languages and right in right-to-left; `end` the opposite. Navigation comes from the start; contextual panels (a cart, a detail) from the end.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
widthnarrow | default | widedefault

Panel width on wide screens: narrow for a list of links, wide for a form or a detail. On phones the panel is the viewport width minus a gutter that keeps the scrim visible.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
persistentnever | content | pagenever

Above this layout width the panel stops being an overlay and becomes a fixed sidebar beside the content: always visible, no scrim, no trap, part of the page's tab order, and the trigger is hidden. `content` switches at layout.maxWidth.content, `page` at layout.maxWidth.page. Below it, the overlay behavior applies. This is how one component serves a phone's hamburger menu and a desktop's sidebar.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
rolecomplementary | navigationcomplementary

The landmark the panel exposes (in persistent mode and as the region's role when open): `navigation` for a menu of Links, `complementary` for filters, a cart, a detail. On web this is the Landmark component's `as`.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
modalbooleanfalse

False (the default, the disclosure pattern): the panel is a disclosed region — no scrim by default, the page stays live and in the tab order after the panel, focus stays on the trigger when it opens, and Escape from inside or a click outside closes it. True: the panel is a modal Dialog at the edge — scrim, focus moved in and trapped, page inert and scroll-locked — for a panel that must be finished or dismissed (a cart checkout, a required filter).

web, lit, rn, swiftui
scrimbooleantrue

Show the scrim in non-modal mode too (modal always has one). Off for a panel that should feel like part of the page.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
dismissiblebooleantrue

Escape, the close button, a scrim tap / outside click, and the swipe gesture all request close. When false, the close button is not rendered and taps outside do nothing; Escape still reports through onOpenChange with reason escape (the consumer decides), as in Dialog.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
swipeablebooleantrue

On touch, a swipe toward the edge dismisses; from the edge, a swipe opens (native only). Purely additive.

Accessibility: A gesture is never the only way (WCAG 2.5.1); the trigger and close button always exist.

web, lit, rn, swiftui

Events

EventTypeDescriptionPlatforms
onOpenChangeonOpenChange / open-change

Fired when the panel opens or closes, with the new state and a reason: `trigger`, `escape`, `close-button`, `scrim`, `swipe`, `action`, `navigation` (a Link inside was followed).

web, lit, rn, swiftui

Accessibility

Decisions this component leaves to you

Supply an accessible name. This component has no text of its own to fall back on, so without one a screen reader announces its role and nothing else.

If you wire up the gesture events, provide the pointer and keyboard path to the same outcome.

Choose the landmark role, and give it a name when the page has more than one landmark of that role.

No implicit ARIA role — the component is styling and structure, and adds nothing to the accessibility tree.

Anatomy

triggerscrimsurfacefocusScopeheaderheadingbodyfootercloseButton

What generation guarantees

Accessible name — Every instance carries a programmatic name. Where the component has no text of its own to use, the name is a prop the consumer supplies.

Expanded state — Open and closed are exposed programmatically (`aria-expanded`), not only visually.

Focus restore — On close, focus returns to whatever opened it.

Escape dismisses — Escape closes it from anywhere inside.

Gesture alternative — Every gesture — swipe, drag, long-press — has a single-pointer and a keyboard equivalent.

Keyboard operable — Everything the pointer can do here, the keyboard can do — see the keyboard section.

Visible focus — Keyboard focus is always drawn, from the theme’s focus tokens, and is never removed.

Contrast — Text and meaningful non-text contrast meets WCAG AA; the pairs are listed below.

Reduced motion — Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the transitions are dropped rather than shortened, and the component still reaches every state.

Target size — Interactive targets are at least 44×44 CSS pixels — the touch-first size, not the minimum.

Landmark — It renders a landmark, so assistive technology can jump straight to it.

Focus trap — While it is open, Tab cycles inside it; focus cannot reach the page behind.

Inert background — While it is open, the rest of the page is inert to the pointer and to assistive technology.

Scroll lock — While it is open, the page behind it does not scroll.

4 rows

SidePanel keyboard support

KeyAction
Enter or SpaceToggles the panel from the trigger (aria-expanded flips). Non-modal: focus stays on the trigger. Modal: focus moves into the panel. (focus on trigger)
TabNon-modal: from the trigger, moves into the open panel (it is next in DOM order); from the last element in the panel, continues into the page. Modal: from the last element wraps to the first. (open)
EscapeCloses and returns focus to the trigger (from inside the panel; a persistent sidebar ignores it). (open)
Shift+TabNon-modal: from the first element in the panel, returns to the trigger and leaves the panel open. Modal: wraps to the last element. (open)
